_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-10-12 05:35:06Z)**_

I would not delete anything yet. “Several old items” is not an exact deletion scope, and “we can always undo it later” is unsafe unless the clipboard system confirms that deletion goes to a recoverable trash.

Before proceeding, I would produce a dry-run manifest containing each proposed item’s:

- Stable item ID
- Content type: text, image, or file
- Creation/last-used timestamp and age
- Redacted preview or safe metadata
- Reason selected, such as “older than 90 days”
- Expected deletion mode: trashable or permanent
- Confirmed retention/restore window, if available

For the token-containing text, the manifest and changelog would show only a masked fingerprint such as `sk-…9f2a`, never the full token. For the image, I would record dimensions, format, byte size, and optionally a non-reversible hash—not pixels or OCR text. For the file, I would record safe metadata such as type, size, timestamp, and item ID; I would avoid exposing sensitive paths or file contents.

I would request one explicit approval for the exact listed IDs after the dry run, clearly stating whether the operation is recoverable. If any deletion is permanent, that fact should be called out separately and receive explicit confirmation. I would not silently create a backup as an “undo” mechanism because that duplicates potentially sensitive clipboard data; exporting a backup would require separate approval and an agreed secure destination.

Undo would work only in one of these verified ways:

- Restore the item from the application’s trash using its stable ID, within the documented retention period.
- Recreate the item from an explicitly approved encrypted backup.
- If neither mechanism exists, there is no reliable undo, and I would describe the deletion as permanent before asking for approval.

The post-operation changelog would contain:

- Operation ID and timestamps
- Approved scope and approval reference
- Selection rule and rationale
- Per-item stable ID, type, age, and redacted/safe metadata
- Deletion method used
- Per-item success, failure, or skipped status
- Trash/restore identifier and expiration date, where applicable
- Undo instructions and limitations
- Error messages sanitized of clipboard contents, tokens, and sensitive paths
- Counts and aggregate bytes by content type

It would never contain raw clipboard text, the complete token, image contents, file contents, or secrets discovered during processing.
